Did you enjoy that? No, I did. I think,  
for us, when you wake up in the morning,  you have some sort of envision of how the  
game is going to be. You're always looking  at the opponent's strengths. Even though  
Aberdeen have struggled lately for their  best form, they still carried a threat.  
Even last week, I thought they had ample  opportunities to score more than one goal.
We tried to play a team with two ball  carriers in the side, a front two,  
and tried to play on the last line as often  as we could. We tried to get Danny and Fraser  
into the game, and I thought we did that  really well. We kept switching the play,  
getting up the pitch, putting balls into  the box, and asking questions of them.
But ultimately, you still need someone to score  a goal. You still need that pressure to count,  
and I thought today, although we've  been more than decent between both boxes  
in recent weeks, it's been pointed out  that we've not scored enough goals,  
and that's valid. We've also not kept enough  clean sheets. I think there's been signs recently,  
apart from the second half at Ibrox, that  we've been a bit more stingy with our work.
I'm delighted to get the clean sheet today  and really liked the level of performance. The  
goal from Big Brad was brilliant. He gets it, and  although he didn't score with the first touch, he  
managed to get it over the line. I thought he led  the line brilliantly. Young Bobby will remember  
playing alongside him—Bobby enjoyed the game as  well. His movement, drifting into good areas, was  
very intelligent for someone so young. He's better  with his back to goal and also facing the play.
All in all, going in at half-time,  you're thinking we should be more than  
one up in terms of opportunities. I've just  watched the first half of Hibs and Hearts,  
and you're looking at Hibs being  totally dominant but going in at  
half-time one each. I spoke at half-time to  reinforce our superiority and try to start  
the second half similarly. Once we got the  second goal, it allowed us to breathe a bit.
Aberdeen made changes—they’ve  got options in forward areas,  
different types of players that make you  think differently about your defending. We  
had to stay sharp, and I thought we were.  For the subs to get two goals as well and  
for Bruce to score, it was almost a perfect  day. It's always important for strikers to  
score goals. Bobby didn't get his goal  today, but he had a very strong game.
When you get that 90 minutes perfect,  what does it do for everybody? 
It puts wind in the sails at the perfect time.  We've spoken about this run of fixtures. I think  
the imbalance in the early season—chopping  and changing with suspensions and juggling  
Europe—has been a challenge. But now, there are  no excuses. We need to reinforce our home form.
We had two away points—got one at Motherwell—and  I said then it’s only a good point if you win  
your home games. It was a lot made about  not getting a penalty at Motherwell,  
which was a real injustice for us. We came  into this game feeling good about ourselves.
It’s Boxing Day, and we’ve been looking  for this strong home performance. Did  
I think we’d score four goals against  a strong team like Aberdeen? Probably  
not. But it's nice to see everything paying  off. Aberdeen have assembled a strong squad,  
spent a lot of money, and  started the season brilliantly.
We spent £120,000 putting our squad together,  so we've got to do so much right to overcome  
a strong team like that. Today, we managed to do  it, and I’m absolutely delighted for the players.
It could have been more than four as well.  Plenty of chances, especially in the second half. 
It could have been, but we’ll take the four. The  clean sheet was vitally important. Aberdeen always  
keep you on your toes—one pass and Duke is 1v1,  or Shandon Morris is coming on, and Jamie McGrath  
always gets chances in every game. You very rarely  keep that type of talent quiet for a full game.
We're delighted that we've managed the clean  sheet as much as the four goals but it still  
doesn't do us any harm to score four goals. I  would have taken a one nil today any sort of win 
get a clean sheet and can through the game unscaithed which I think we have  
um so it was a strong performance for us and it  has to be to beat um a team like Aberdeen. You  
had to try and keep in top of them because  if you if you let up at any point Aberdeen  
are good enough to pick holes through you  they're a well-managed team the managers  
done a brilliant job um so we're delighted that  we've managed to overcome such a strong opponent  
four goals of real exceptional quality as well particular through the second half
We kept switching the play brilliantly in  the first half. Brad led the line well,  
Bobby was exposing space, and Danny Armstrong was  back to his best. Fraser was terrific on the other  
side. We put a lot of crosses into the box, made  Aberdeen defend, and got loads of set plays.
Big David Watson came up with a brilliant  goal. He’s so good at timing his runs,  
which is a skill that will determine what  level he reaches. Once we got the second goal,  
it allowed us to stay on the job. It was a perfect  finish with Brucey getting his goal as well.
Bruce was unlucky not to start today,  but the shape suited the team we played.  
Three strikers scored, and Bobby was  outstanding. I’m delighted all around.
title: Derek McInnes Post Match Press Conference | Kilmarnock 4-0 Aberdeen
